title: Time domain Stokes mechanism of pair correlated k gap solitons in nonlinear photonic time crystal slabs
authors: Jiaxiang Sun, Guowei Chen, Liang Zhang, Yiming Pan
abstract: Pair generation in time-varying media is commonly attributed to time reflection at temporal boundaries or to amplification inside momentum k gaps. Here we show that these two processes are connected by the time domain Stokes phenomenon. A finite duration photonic time crystal (PTC) slab provides the necessary Stokes connection between the incident vacuum mode, transient k gap amplification, and time boundary scattering. With Kerr nonlinearity, the otherwise unbounded amplification is arrested, spawning Kerr stabilized k gap solitons. When these solitons cross the exit boundary of the time slab, Stokes induced mode conversion produces a secondary pair generation process, yielding four spatially separated and entangled pulse branches. Detection of a backward propagating light pulse therefore heralds its forward propagating partner. We further propose combined Hanbury Brown Twiss and Hong Ou Mandel measurements to test their nonclassical correlations. These results reveal a link between asymptotic Stokes physics and quantum temporal scattering in PTCs, and suggest a route toward ultrafast heralded quantum light sources.
summary: The research shows that nonlinear photonic time crystals can generate entangled photon pairs by exploiting the time-domain Stokes phenomenon. This process involves k-gap soliton formation followed by secondary splitting at the slab's exit boundary. By measuring quantum correlations, they confirm this mechanism provides a route for ultrafast, heralded sources of nonclassical light.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish a unified connection between two mechanisms of pair generation—time reflection at temporal boundaries and parametric amplification within momentum k-gaps—using the time-domain Stokes phenomenon.
main_result: They demonstrate that in nonlinear photonic time crystal slabs, the secondary Stokes conversion occurring at the exit boundary splits stable k-gap solitons into four spatially separated, entangled pulse branches.
method: The study combines theoretical analysis using Airy functions to model Stokes asymptotics with numerical simulations (FDTD) and quantum characterization via second-order correlation measurements (HBT/HOM).
model_or_system: The system is a nonlinear Photonic Time Crystal (PTC) slab governed by an electrodynamic wave equation incorporating Kerr nonlinearity. The dynamics are analyzed through the lens of the Stokes phenomenon, connecting linear Floquet theory to nonlinear soliton formation.
key_observables: Second-order correlation functions ($g_{HBT}^{(2)}, g_{HOM}^{(2)}$), which confirm nonclassical correlations and entanglement; detection of backward-propagating pulses heralding forward partners.
important_parameters: Kerr nonlinearity strength ($ eta$), modulation depth ($	ilde{\delta}$ or $r$), and the time duration of the active PTC window.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mapping the system dynamics to the Airy equation near turning points, treating the process as a temporal analogue of standard Stokes scattering theory.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the macroscopic time-domain Stokes phenomenon leading to pair generation, showing spatiotemporal splitting into four branches, and demonstrating the dependence of entanglement on the PTC modulation depth.
paper_structure: The paper develops from establishing the theoretical link via the Stokes phenomenon (Airy connection) to simulating nonlinear dynamics in a finite-time slab, culminating in quantum characterization using HBT/HOM measurements to confirm nonclassical pair correlations.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it bridges classical wave asymptotics (Stokes theory) with quantum light generation mechanisms (parametric amplification), offering a pathway for on-demand entangled photon sources using engineered periodic media.
